blocks.text: Santiago to Torres del Paine via Puerto Natales

The transfer to the airport takes about **40 minutes**. From there, fly to Puerto Natales.

On arrival, transfer to Torres del Paine National Park, a journey of around **2 hours**. Check in at your hotel inside the park, across from Grey Glacier.

Today marks the start of the main Patagonian leg of the journey. The city gives way to lakes, open steppe, granite mountains and glaciers.
Colourful houses on the Puerto Natales waterfront with mountains in the background, Chile

Breakfast at the hotel, followed by a tour of the national park lasting around **8 hours**.

The granite towers of Paine rise more than 2,000 m above the steppe. Before the national park was established in 1959, the land was used extensively for sheep grazing and took a long time to recover from the pressure.

The park has been part of UNESCO’s network of biosphere reserves since 1978. Rheas, Andean condors, flamingos and other birds live here. You may also spot guanacos on the open plains, where their herds have grown considerably after years of protection from poaching.

The route includes Milodón Cave on Benítez Hill, about **25 km from Puerto Natales**. In 1895, remains of prehistoric animals were found here, including a sabre-toothed cat, an American horse and a giant ground sloth. The cave takes its name from Mylodon darwini, which lived here 8,000–10,000 years ago. A sculpture of the animal stands at the entrance.

Torres del Paine covers more than **242,000 hectares**. Inside the park, open steppe gives way to lakes, waterfalls, forest and ice-covered peaks. A short walk of about 15 minutes leads to Salto Grande, the waterfall between Lakes Nordenskjöld and Pehoé.

On the way back, you’ll pass the Serrano River and Lakes Toro and Porteño. Overnight at the hotel.
